core_obligations: Record that the diagonal is a Koszul-regular immersion, hence perfect proper, so that its right adjoint c exists (proof lines 3891-3900).
Run the four term chain expressing O_X, ending with the factor wedge^d(N_Delta)[-d] (proof lines 3902-3920).
Invert the invertible object to obtain a(O_S) = wedge^d(C_Delta)[d] and identify the conormal sheaf with Omega_{X/S} (proof lines 3922-3931).
proof_roadmap: The diagonal and its properties (proof lines 3891-3900).
Inversion and the identification of the conormal sheaf (proof lines 3922-3931).
difficulty_reason: For a Noetherian scheme S and a smooth proper morphism f : X -> S of relative dimension d with right adjoint a of Rf_*, the lemma asserts an isomorphism wedge^d Omega_{X/S}[d] -> a(O_S) in D(O_X) (statement lines 3878-3889). The proof sets omega = a(O_S), lets c be the right adjoint for the diagonal Delta : X -> X x_S X, and notes that since Delta is the diagonal of a smooth morphism it is a Koszul-regular immersion by Divisors, Lemma labelled divisors-lemma-immersion-smooth-into-smooth-regular-immersion, hence a perfect proper morphism by More on Morphisms, Lemma labelled more-morphisms-lemma-regular-immersion-perfect (proof lines 3891-3900). It then computes O_X by a four term chain: the pre-rigid identity equation labelled equation-pre-rigid, the comparison lemma Lemma labelled lemma-compare-with-pullback-flat-proper-noetherian, the fact that pr_1 o Delta = id_X, and Lemma labelled lemma-regular-immersion which identifies the remaining factor with wedge^d(N_Delta)[-d] (proof lines 3902-3920). Since wedge^d(N_Delta) is invertible, the conclusion follows by inverting the invertible object wedge^d(N_Delta)[-d], and the conormal sheaf of the diagonal is Omega_{X/S} by Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-differentials-diagonal (proof lines 3922-3931). Recognising the pre-rigid identity as the statement that the relative dualizing complex times the top exterior power of the conormal sheaf of the diagonal is trivial, and then inverting that invertible object, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
